Evaluate a declared allocation model at supplied fixed parameters

Source: R/06-ae_workflow.R
evaluate_allocation.Rd

Solves once and constructs compact coverage from the saved evaluated outputs. The existing equilibrium result carries its prediction snapshot; adding coverage does not retain the original model or create a scenario type. The caller changes system supply/demand by preparing a new model explicitly.

Usage

evaluate_allocation(model, theta, coverage_args = list(), ...)

Arguments

model

A corrected CLM declared over checked prepared inputs.

theta

A complete model parameter vector. Named parameters align to the model contract; unnamed values follow its declared order. This operation estimates no parameters and is not a causal intervention estimator. For a model with demand groups, a parameter held fixed by clm_allocation(fixed = ) may be given only with its fixed value, and unknown names are an error.

coverage_args

Named reporting controls for compact coverage, including optional norm, units, reporting floors and classification cuts. A norm must have the same declared supply-per-demand scale as capacity attribution.

...

Named controls passed to the existing fixed-parameter solver, including requested_outputs. For a model with demand groups, request the per-group outputs here, for example requested_outputs = c("utilization_by_group", "access_by_group", "outside_share_by_group"); the other outputs are pooled over the groups (demand-weighted). A group's own access and outside share are NA on rows where that group has no demand and its travel there is not usable.

The expected counts that can be requested with requested_outputs are flow (origins by facilities), flow_outside (flow with one more column, "(outside)", holding each origin's expected outside count D_i * outside_share_i), utilization_outside (utilization with one more element, "(outside)", the expected outside count of all origins) and, with demand groups, utilization_by_group and utilization_outside_by_group (with one more row, "(outside)", the expected outside count of each group). The outside counts are zero for a model without an outside option; they are the outputs that fit_allocation() fits to observed outside counts.

Value

The existing ae_equilibrium with its portable prediction snapshot (none for a model with demand groups, which cannot be predicted yet) and compact coverage. Coverage uses raw supply units without kappa; proportional attributed capacity is not a delivered-service measure or a hard constraint on expected utilization.

See also

Other allocation steps: bootstrap_fit(), calc_demand(), calc_travel_time(), check_fit(), clm_allocation(), compare_fits(), decay_kernel(), fit_allocation(), huff_allocation(), predict_allocation(), prepare_allocation()
